items.statement: uct_ib_iface_dev_addr_is_reachable unpacks the remote device address, validates PKEY compatibility, and dispatches matching Ethernet link layers to the RoCE reachability classifier.
For RoCE peers, the classifier handles wildcard or all mode first, then checks RoCE version and RoCEv2 address family and GID conversion before selecting route or local-subnet evaluation.
A wildcard remote RoCE version or reachability mode all returns reachable before further RoCE checks.
Different concrete local and remote RoCE versions enter the unreachable branch.
Matching RoCE peers whose version is not RoCE v2 are assumed reachable without address-family or route checks.
RoCE v2 classification enters the address-family mismatch branch when local and remote families differ.
RoCE v2 classification enters the invalid-local-GID branch when conversion of the local GID to a socket address fails.
RoCE v2 classification enters the invalid-remote-GID branch when conversion of the remote GID to a socket address fails.
A valid RoCE v2 peer in route mode is evaluated by route reachability.
A valid RoCE v2 peer in local_subnet mode is evaluated by subnet comparison.
RoCE initialization stores local_subnet as the effective reachability mode when the legacy override is enabled, otherwise it stores the configured mode.
The stored subnet-prefix length is forced to zero unless the interface is RoCE v2 in local_subnet mode.
Successful automatic prefix discovery stores the netdevice mask length in addr_prefix_bits.
Failure to resolve the RoCE netdevice makes automatic prefix discovery set addr_prefix_bits to zero.
Failure to query the netdevice mask makes automatic prefix discovery set addr_prefix_bits to zero.
Interface construction acquires GID information, optional completion-channel state, statistics, and TX/RX CQs, while failure labels and cleanup destroy those resources in reverse dependency order.
A PKEY partition-value mismatch returns unreachable before link-layer classification.
When neither endpoint has full PKEY membership, reachability returns false before link-layer classification.
Only matching local and remote Ethernet link layers enter RoCE reachability; an IB/RoCE link-layer mismatch is unreachable.
A zero-bit local-subnet prefix treats every remote address as reachable.
The local_subnet gtest sends an active message between two endpoints, flushes outstanding work, waits for the receive counter to advance, and verifies the received length and payload.
Failure to resolve a RoCE netdevice records a no-ndev reason and returns unreachable.
When neither the RoCE netdevice, loopback, nor a kernel local route accepts the remote address, route mode records the attempted route sources and returns unreachable.
A concrete RoCE version mismatch records the local and remote GID versions and returns unreachable.
A RoCE v2 address-family mismatch records both families and returns unreachable.
Local GID conversion failure records the invalid local GID and returns unreachable.
Remote GID conversion failure records the invalid remote GID and returns unreachable.
An IB/RoCE link-layer mismatch records both endpoint link layers and returns unreachable.
UCX identifies RoCE by the Ethernet link-layer flag: matching local and remote Ethernet endpoints use RoCE reachability rules, whereas an IB/RoCE link-layer mismatch is unreachable.
items.description: Matching local and remote Ethernet link layers delegate to RoCE reachability checks, while mismatched IB and RoCE link layers are unreachable.

items.statement: During RoCE address-prefix initialization, enabling the legacy rocev2_local_subnet option replaces the configured reachability mode with local_subnet for backward compatibility.
items.description: For backward compatibility, the legacy rocev2_local_subnet setting overrides the configured reachability mode to local_subnet.
